descriptions.text: Enchanted Roll of Never-ending Duct Tape. Fifty meters. Odds are good you know who Ted Bundy is. Odds are even better you don't know who Vesta Stoudt is. And while this problem is not exclusive to you hairless monkeys and your pollution-ridden world, those first two statements are part of the reason why you have received this prize. Will you use it to tie people up? Will you use it to save the lives of those you love? Will you wrap your ankles together and sensuously rub your supple feet up and down a dungeon wall while you run your hands through your hair? Who knows! …

beats.headline: Finally, the tape
beats.text: Alone with Donut in the crafting room before the raid, Carl opens his two new boxes. The silver boss box for killing Ruckus holds twenty-five more surefires and a bottle of Jellyfish Salve. Then the silver fan box from the end of the last floor. Yes, he says. Finally. Thanks, guys. It is a thick, enchanted roll of duct tape, fifty metres that grow back, and he already has a use in mind. He takes it to his sapper's table.

beats.headline: Better than rope
beats.text: With about forty-five minutes left, the raid leaves Hump Town by the main gate, and on the Chariot's raised back seat sits the struggling form of Wynne the dirigible gnome. Carl had planned to tie him with rope, but duct tape works much better. In front of the landed gnomes Carl pours a vial of Mountain Dew down "Wynne's" throat, then throws the duct-taped form over his shoulder and trudges toward their wicker basket, praying none of the gnomes notice that the back seat of the Chariot is gone, or that Wynne is about two feet longer than he should be.

beats.headline: Katia under the tape
beats.text: Under the duct tape, "Wynne" is mostly Katia. She is shaped as the whole back seat of the Chariot, which Carl had to remove for this to work, and as the body of the gnome sitting on it, her real eyes in among the tape for a wide, raised view of the situation. She is Henrik's body in the cart behind as well. The bulk of the plan rests, once again, on Donut's charm bonus and Katia's shapeshifting.

beats.headline: Taped into the minifridge
beats.text: On the submarine's bridge the commentators expect the rest of the depth charges to be duds, and the display window looks about to break. Carl yanks the fuse from a hob-lobber, replaces it with hobgoblin pus, and tapes a potion bottle to the bomb with his duct tape, a crude cousin of something more elegant in the cookbook. He has no idea whether it will work. He looks for a place safe from the first rush of water, puts the bomb in the bolted-down minifridge beside the captain's chair, and duct-tapes the door closed.

beats.headline: Mending the net
beats.text: On the roof of the flying house, with the wind picking up, Louis is desperately mending the net of ropes, and the patch is not going to hold for long. He tosses the empty roll of magical duct tape back down to Carl, so high that Carl has to jump for it. He catches it. Barely. He would have throttled Louis if it had gone over the edge, and he puts the roll back in his inventory to regenerate.

beats.headline: A rocket on Samantha's head
beats.text: Samantha's head sits on the ground with her jaw held all the way open, like she is getting a root canal, and a rocket tied to the side of it with duct tape wrapped round her forehead and her neck. This is one of the few things Carl could not test in his workshop. He pulls out his xistera extension and tells her not to close her mouth until she sees them or the catapult. Okay, says Samantha. Click. The missile launches her into the air like a bottle rocket.
